metadata.title: Word Frequency Count
metadata.description: Tally word occurrences into a dictionary with a loop.

instructions.main: Given `words = ["apple", "banana", "apple", "cherry", "banana", "apple"]`, count how often each word occurs in a dictionary named `counts`.
steps: Loop over `words`; for each word add 1 to its count.

hints.message: Start with `counts = {}`, loop over `words`, and bump each word's count by 1.
`counts[word]` reads the stored value — on the first sighting the key isn't there yet, so `counts[word] + 1` raises KeyError. Use `counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1` so missing keys start at 0.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: Your dictionary counts every word correctly.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: After running, `counts` must be {"apple": 3, "banana": 2, "cherry": 1} — every word's count has to land in the dictionary without raising KeyError.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You insert each count with an assignment like counts[word] = ...
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Store each count with a key assignment: `counts[word] = ...`.
